land.text: Babylon: 'It was held at Babylon in June 323 BC'; Perdiccas became 'Regent of the Empire' there

predecessors.note: Cliopatria places the Perdiccas row under the Macedonian Empire umbrella.

land.text: Babylonia, held by the empire after the regent's death: Seleucus 'only became satrap of Babylonia at the second partition (the Partition of Triparadisus)'

successors.note: macedonian-empire /ledger/47-48 gives Babylonia to Seleucus as the empire's satrap (a vassal tint) from Triparadisus until 312. The Perdiccas page has Archon as satrap of Babylon, then 'Docimus conquered Babylon and killed Archon in battle' (undated).

land.text: Cliopatria's first Seleucid shape (318-316) has the same bounding box as Perdiccas's

successors.note: Cliopatria's reading only, and later: the Seleucid row starts in 318, the macedonian-empire dossier has Seleucus as the empire's satrap in between, and Seleucus is independent in Babylon from 312.

capitals.name: Babylon
capitals.note: Perdiccas 'had chosen to centre the empire at Babylon', as Alexander had; Babylon is the only seat the page names.

correction.text: The Cliopatria shape, unchanged, but ending in 320 BC, when Perdiccas was killed ('probably in the summer of 320 BC', Perdiccas page), not in 319

keyframe_review.note: 117 k km2 on Babylonia (Iraq, with Elam and Kuwait fringes): the seat of the regency, since Perdiccas 'effectively ruled Alexander's increasingly unstable empire' from Babylon and 'had chosen to centre the empire at Babylon'. It is a reading, not a satrapy: the Partition of Babylon page assigns Babylonia to Archon (probably), so the regent's own lands were the imperial court and army, not a province. Cliopatria's end in 319 is a year late; the page has Perdiccas killed in 320. Neither page gives an area to compare. [Reviewer me-05-b: verdict adjust, since the dossier ends in 320 and the Cliopatria row in 319.]

region.text: Babylon and Babylonia, the seat of the regency

ledger.note: 323: At the Partition of Babylon, 'held at Babylon in June 323 BC', Perdiccas becomes Regent of the Empire (epimeletes) and holds the council 'as Hegemon' that assigns the satrapies. The page does not give him land of his own; the region is the seat of the regency.

region.text: Babylon and Babylonia, the seat of the regency

ledger.note: 323: the regency's Babylonia counts as the empire's own tint. 'It was held at Babylon in June 323 BC'; Perdiccas as epimeletes 'insisted on the supreme authority in the name of the king' (Partition of Babylon page); the page gives Babylonia to Archon (probably). The page does not make the regent's seat a province, so the vassal relation is the macedonian-empire dossier's model (its /ledger/42, confidence 2), followed here at confidence 2.

region.text: Babylon and Babylonia, the seat of the regency

ledger.note: 320: the regency ends with Perdiccas's death. 'killed him in 320 BC when the invasion foundered'; 'probably in the summer of 320 BC' (Perdiccas page). macedonian-empire /ledger/47 ends the same vassalage in 321, at Triparadisus (Partition of Triparadisus page, 321 BC); the Perdiccas page's 320 is one year later, and eu-02 is asked to align.

region.text: Babylon and Babylonia, the seat of the regency

ledger.note: 320: Perdiccas is murdered by his officers. His soldiers 'mutinied and killed him in 320 BC when the invasion [of Egypt] foundered', 'probably in the summer of 320 BC'; the regency passed to Peithon and Arrhidaeus, then to Antipater at Triparadisus. The land passes to the empire's own satrapy: Seleucus is satrap of Babylonia from Triparadisus ('It is well established that Seleucus only became satrap of Babylonia at the second partition', Partition of Babylon page; macedonian-empire /ledger/48).

wars.name: Perdiccas' campaign in Cappadocia

zones.text: Cappadocia, the satrapy of Ariarathes I

wars.outcome: 'in the early summer of 322 BC Perdiccas marched with the imperial army'; he defeated the satrap Ariarathes I in two battles, then took him captive, tortured and killed him.
wars.note: An act of the empire's regent; it moved no land into Perdiccas's own shape.

wars.name: Perdiccas' invasion of Egypt
wars.outcome: Failed at the Nile crossings; the army mutinied and killed Perdiccas in 320. It followed Ptolemy's diversion of Alexander's body to Egypt (late 321) and his conquest of Cyrenaica 'without Perdiccas' approval'.
wars.note: The Wars of the Diadochi infobox calls this the First War (321-319).

certainty.note: The seat of an imperial regency has no borders drawn by any page.

sources.title: Perdiccas
sources.note: Regency, Babylon as seat, Cappadocia 322, the invasion of Egypt, death 320.

sources.title: Partition of Babylon
sources.note: June 323, the satrapy assignments (Babylonia to Archon, probably), Perdiccas as regent. Reopened in the repair pass for the vassal events: Seleucus satrap of Babylonia only at Triparadisus.

sources.title: Partition of Triparadisus
sources.note: Repair pass: 321 BC, Antipater regent, 'Babylonia, on Seleucus' (no year for the assignment); cited in the vassal_end note for the one-year difference from macedonian-empire /ledger/47.

notes: Page budget two pages. This is a regency, not a territorial state: Cliopatria draws Babylonia for it, and the shape is kept as the seat of the regency, but the regent's authority covered the whole Macedonian Empire (the macedonian-empire dossier). The end year is 320 on the Perdiccas article (Cliopatria 319). Not settled: who held Babylonia after 320 (Cliopatria's Seleucid Empire row starts in 318 with the same outline; the Partition of Babylon page, reopened in the repair pass, says 'It is well established that Seleucus only became satrap of Babylonia at the second partition (the Partition of Triparadisus)', 321 on that page's date); the Partition page's own uncertainty over Archon, Peucestas or Seleucus as the satrap of Babylonia. No ledger events beyond birth and end: the pages opened give no territorial gains or losses for the regency itself. Repair pass (2026-10-19): added vassal_start (June 323) and vassal_end (320) with counterpart macedonian-empire, mirroring macedonian-empire /ledger/42 and /ledger/47 rather than asking eu-02 to drop them: the regency row is kept as the empire's tinted seat. The empire dossier ends it in 321 (Triparadisus) against 320 here (the Perdiccas page); eu-02 is asked to align. The dissolve and the first successor now name macedonian-empire (Seleucus as satrap); seleucid-empire stays as the later holder from Cliopatria's 318 shape. Not agreed with eu-02 in advance.
